uses.issue: Core statutory ground: whether post-9 June 1952 subletting, assignment, or parting with possession occurred without the landlord's written consent.
uses.law_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord;
uses.reason: This is the supplied Delhi provision that directly defines the fixed eviction ground. The record contains opposing positions on exclusive possession, licence versus subletting, and whether the 1944 lease or later conduct supplied written consent.
uses.standalone_value: Supplies the threshold elements and the 9 June 1952 temporal boundary, but does not itself resolve whether respondents had exclusive possession, whether the transaction was a licence, or whether a qualifying written consent existed.
uses.incremental_value: It is the anchor for evaluating section 16's lawfulness rules and the supplied Delhi precedents on assignment/parting with possession; other units cannot displace its express written-consent requirement without a demonstrated applicable override.
uses.limits: Current Indian Kanoon statutory reproduction; historical version is unverified, other section 14 grounds are excluded, and no target judicial interpretation is embedded in this unit.

uses.issue: Whether the Andhra Pradesh rent-control text itself governs the Delhi section 14(1)(b) ground.
uses.reason: The unit sets out Andhra Pradesh Act section 10(ii)(a) and section 2(ix), while the fixed question is under the Delhi Rent Control Act. The supplied record itself flags that legal requirements under another tenancy statute differ from Delhi law.
uses.standalone_value: It can show the elements of the quoted Andhra Pradesh regime only; it supplies no Delhi rule for the present ground.
uses.incremental_value: No additional controlling value for the current Delhi issue was found once the Delhi statutory units are present; any analogy would require a judicial bridge rather than direct use of this statute.
uses.limits: Different jurisdiction and statute; historical quoted text only, with no certification that its conditions map to Delhi section 14(1)(b).

uses.issue: How a company amalgamation may be characterized as a transfer of tenancy and why written consent can matter in a rent-control setting.
uses.reason: The Supreme Court treated a company-proposed amalgamation as transferring the tenant company's interest and possession under the Andhra Pradesh Act. That is contextual for the record's bank-amalgamation history, but it does not itself decide the Delhi ground or establish the legal mechanism of either bank amalgamation here.
uses.standalone_value: Supports only the general proposition that an amalgamation can operate as a tenancy transfer in the specific AP-law and scheme context before that Court.
uses.incremental_value: Adds an amalgamation-transfer analogy to the Delhi statutory text and reported Delhi precedent, but remains secondary because the target record does not identify a matching company-law mechanism or written-consent status for the bank successions.
uses.limits: Judicially adopted application under Andhra Pradesh law and a specific company amalgamation; not a Delhi holding and not proof of how Pratap Bank, Lakshmi Commercial Bank, or Canara Bank succeeded to this tenancy.

uses.issue: Scope of Delhi section 14(b) as extending beyond consensual subleases to assignment or other modes of parting with possession.
uses.reason: This Supreme Court passage reports a prior Delhi Rent Control Act holding that section 14(b) is broad enough to cover assignment or another mode of parting with possession, including an involuntary sale. It directly informs the statutory phrase relied on in the fixed question.
uses.standalone_value: Supports a broad reading of assignment/parting with possession under Delhi law, but does not determine whether these respondents' occupancy or the historical bank amalgamations fit that category.
uses.incremental_value: Extends the bare statutory wording of section 14(1)(b) by showing that transfer can be broader than a conventional sublease; it is especially relevant if bank succession is argued as an assignment route.
uses.limits: The unit is General Radio's report of Parasaram, not the independently supplied full Parasaram opinion; its factual setting involved liquidation sale, not these bank amalgamations or alleged occupancies.

uses.issue: Whether a protected tenancy/licensee status can pre-exist and survive later statutory acquisition in a different rent regime.
uses.reason: The unit concerns a Bombay Rent Act protected licensee and later statutory acquisition of Esso's interests. It provides context that succession consequences can depend on an independently created protected status and special acquisition statute, but the target record supplies no matching Bombay-law status or Esso-type acquisition.
uses.standalone_value: Shows only that, in its own statutory setting, an existing licence/protected-tenancy status materially affected the later vesting analysis.
uses.incremental_value: Helps limit overgeneralization from amalgamation cases by illustrating that tenancy succession may turn on the source statute and pre-existing status; it does not add a Delhi section 14(1)(b) element.
uses.limits: Bombay Rent Act and Esso acquisition context; no demonstrated application to the Delhi premises or the 1961/1985 bank successions.

uses.issue: Effect of an express special-statute vesting clause that makes a successor the lessee or tenant.
uses.reason: The unit shows a specific acquisition statute expressly vesting tenancy in government and then a government company. It is relevant context for distinguishing statutory succession from ordinary assignment, but the supplied record does not identify an equivalent vesting provision for either bank amalgamation.
uses.standalone_value: Supports tenancy succession only under the specific Esso Acquisition Act/Bombay Rent Act framework described.
uses.incremental_value: When read with the Delhi amalgamation materials, it shows why the precise legal source of a merger or vesting can matter; without a matching statute or scheme in the target record, it cannot resolve the fixed ground.
uses.limits: Specific Esso Acquisition Act, notification, section 396 amalgamation, and Bombay Rent Act section 15A; not a general Delhi eviction immunity.

uses.issue: Counter-position that court-ordered amalgamation vesting may occur without landlord consent and may fall outside section 14(1)(b), while the actual eviction issue remains reserved.
uses.law_quote: would be outside the mischief of the provisions of s. 14(1)(b) of the Rent Control Act.
uses.reason: The Delhi High Court states a prima facie view favorable to vesting on amalgamation without landlord consent, but immediately says it is not deciding whether such transfer amounts to assignment attracting section 14(1)(b) and preserves the landlord's plea. It therefore limits any categorical merger-equals-eviction route.
uses.standalone_value: Supports only a provisional counterargument about amalgamation vesting and confirms that the section 14(1)(b) consequence requires decision in the proper rent-control proceeding.
uses.incremental_value: Directly tempers the broader transfer reasoning in the supplied General Radio/Parasaram material by preserving an unresolved Delhi-specific question about amalgamation and assignment.
uses.limits: Prima facie and expressly reserved; partial document, specific company-scheme context, and no showing that either target bank amalgamation used the same mechanism.

uses.issue: Possible statutory mechanism for voluntary amalgamation of banking companies and transfer/vesting under a sanctioned scheme.
uses.reason: Section 44A supplies one banking-law route by which a sanctioned amalgamation can bind the banks and transfer property and liabilities. Because the record merely states two historical amalgamations and does not identify section 44A or the governing schemes, the unit provides mechanism context only.
uses.standalone_value: Shows what section 44A can do for an amalgamation sanctioned under that section; it does not establish that the 1961 or 1985 target succession occurred under section 44A or transferred this lease on particular terms.
uses.incremental_value: Useful for testing whether an asserted bank succession rests on a statutory vesting mechanism rather than ordinary assignment, but it needs the actual historical scheme/order before it can affect section 14(1)(b).
uses.limits: Official consolidation as amended through a modern snapshot with historical version unverified; distinct from section 45 and from acquisition-act schemes.

uses.issue: Possible RBI/Central Government reconstruction or amalgamation mechanism with statutory transfer, vesting, and override effects.
uses.law_quote: stand transferred to, and vest in
uses.reason: Section 45 describes a special reconstruction/amalgamation scheme that can transfer assets and liabilities and override contrary laws or instruments. It could matter if a target bank succession occurred under such a scheme, but the supplied case does not identify section 45, a moratorium, or a relevant sanctioned scheme.
uses.standalone_value: Supplies the structure and legal effects of a section 45 scheme only; it cannot establish that the target tenancy vested under this route.
uses.incremental_value: Complements the Delhi rent units by identifying a possible special-law source of vesting that would need to be reconciled with section 14(1)(b) if proved applicable.
uses.limits: Modern official consolidation with historical version unverified; actual scheme terms and historical applicability to the 1961/1985 bank amalgamations are absent.

uses.issue: Possible Central Government scheme power to amalgamate or transfer undertakings of corresponding new banks and vest assets and liabilities.
uses.reason: Section 9 supplies another bank-specific scheme mechanism, including transfer and vesting effects, that could matter to a nationalised-bank succession. The allowed record does not identify a section 9 scheme governing the 1985 Lakshmi Commercial Bank-to-Canara Bank succession.
uses.standalone_value: Establishes only the statutory power and effects of a scheme made under the 1980 Acquisition Act; it does not prove a target-specific scheme or lease transfer.
uses.incremental_value: Adds a potential statutory-vesting route that should prevent assuming all bank amalgamations are ordinary assignments, but has no operative value without the actual applicable scheme.
uses.limits: Historical version is unverified and OCR is uncorrected; the unit concerns corresponding new banks and does not itself identify the legal instrument used in the target bank history.

uses.issue: Example of a bank-specific amalgamation scheme expressly deeming the transferee bank to become lessee of leased property.
uses.reason: The 1993 New Bank of India scheme demonstrates that a specific banking amalgamation instrument can expressly address leased property and successor-lessee status. It is contextual only because it concerns different banks and a later date.
uses.standalone_value: Supports only the legal effect of the New Bank of India-to-Punjab National Bank scheme, including its lease treatment; it says nothing directly about Pratap Bank, Lakshmi Commercial Bank, or Canara Bank.
uses.incremental_value: Shows why the actual target amalgamation scheme matters and why generic merger labels are insufficient; it cannot substitute for the missing target-specific instrument.
uses.limits: Official 1993 scheme for New Bank of India and Punjab National Bank only; no automatic application to other bank mergers.

uses.issue: Lawfulness of subletting before versus after 9 June 1952 and the requirement of written consent for later subletting or assignment.
uses.law_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord
uses.reason: Section 16 directly supplies date-sensitive rules for when subletting is deemed lawful and when previous written consent is required. The record claims very old occupancies but does not pin every alleged subtenancy to the statutory date boundaries.
uses.standalone_value: Can classify the legal significance of a proved subletting date and written-consent status, including the pre-9 June 1952 deeming rule; it cannot determine those facts from the statute alone.
uses.incremental_value: Refines section 14(1)(b) by separating pre-9 June 1952 subletting from later subletting and by confirming the written-consent requirement for later periods.
uses.limits: Current statutory reproduction with historical version unverified; the allowed record does not establish a precise creation date for each respondent's occupancy or subtenancy.

uses.issue: Notice procedure for subtenancies created with written consent and for pre-Act lawful subtenancies.
uses.law_quote: with the previous consent in writing of the landlord
uses.reason: Section 17 regulates notice of subtenancy and a dispute procedure. The parties dispute whether notice requirements matter here, but the supplied text does not make section 17 notice an element of the section 14(1)(b) eviction ground itself.
uses.standalone_value: Supplies notice timing and procedure for qualifying subtenancies; alone it does not establish or defeat the fixed section 14(1)(b) ground.
uses.incremental_value: Helps separate the written-consent question under sections 14(1)(b)/16 from later notice and subtenant-protection issues, especially given the parties' competing submissions about sections 16-18.
uses.limits: Historical version unverified; the allowed record gives argument about notice but no complete notice record, and this unit does not by itself state that missing notice proves the section 14(1)(b) ground.

uses.issue: Whether post-eviction deemed direct tenancy of a protected subtenant answers the threshold section 14(1)(b) ground.
uses.law_quote: Where an order for eviction in respect of any premises is made under section 14
uses.reason: Section 18 addresses what happens to certain subtenants after an eviction order or after pre-Act termination of the head tenancy. The fixed question asks whether the section 14(1)(b) ground is supported, so this consequence provision does not answer that threshold issue on the supplied scope.
uses.standalone_value: Supports potential direct-tenancy consequences for a qualifying subtenant after specified events; it does not establish subletting, assignment, parting with possession, or lack of written consent.
uses.incremental_value: No additional value for deciding the fixed ground once sections 14(1)(b), 16, and 17 are available, except to explain why notice/protection questions may arise after an eviction order.
uses.limits: Consequence/protection provision, not a supplied element of the threshold ground; historical version unverified and no final eviction outcome is part of the allowed record.

coverage_limits: The allowed case record states that Pratap Bank amalgamated with Lakshmi Commercial Bank in 1961 and Lakshmi Commercial Bank with Canara Bank in 1985, but it does not identify the statutory provision, scheme, order, or lease-transfer terms governing either amalgamation.

The alleged occupancies of respondents 2-6 are described as longstanding, but the supplied segments do not establish a precise creation date for each alleged subtenancy relative to 9 June 1952 or commencement of the Delhi Rent Control Act.

The record contains competing claims about exclusive possession, licence status, the 1944 lease, rent receipts, acquiescence, and written consent; the allowed scope does not supply the target court's final reasoning or outcome resolving those disputes.

Several supplied authorities arise under Andhra Pradesh or Bombay rent law, company amalgamation, liquidation, acquisition statutes, or unrelated banking schemes; they cannot be treated as automatically controlling Delhi section 14(1)(b).
The supplied Delhi amalgamation passage in Telesound is expressly prima facie and reserves the section 14(1)(b) eviction question.
The statutory reproductions and consolidations carry stated historical-version limitations; no external historical consolidation, later authority, or omitted provision may be imported.
